_comment: THE CROSS-SECTOR FUNDER PASS, brief 11 item 3. Rung 4 asks whether A FUNDER HAS
PUBLISHED AN AWARD NAMING THE PROJECT, and until this pass that question had only
been asked of hydrogen.
ONCE A LIST IS READ, RUNG 4 IS `searched: true` FOR EVERY ENTRY THE LIST COVERS,
and absence from it is a fail rather than a not_searched. That is brief 12's rule
(D-L2) and this file is what makes it true of the other four sectors.
THE LIST READ HERE IS THE INNOVATION FUND'S OWN PROJECT TABLE -- 413 projects
across every call and every sector, with the call, the sector, the country and the
status, and for 280 of them a project factsheet PDF carrying THE COORDINATOR AND
THE GRANT AMOUNT. 163 factsheets were read: every one whose sector or category or
technology pathway could touch cement, steel, batteries, CO2 transport and storage
or hydrogen. THE TABLE IS THE LIST AND THE FACTSHEET IS THE AWARD.
sources/hydrogen_funder_pass.json IS NOT SUPERSEDED AND IS NOT COPIED. Its 16
programmes and 55 awards -- the three Hydrogen Bank auctions, the four hydrogen
IPCEIs, and the national programmes -- stand as read, and build_ladder.py goes on
scoring hydrogen from them. This file adds the funders that reach the other four.
A MATCH IS BY IDENTIFIER OR BY A DOCUMENT NAMING BOTH, NEVER BY A NAME STEM. Every
match below says which, in `matched_on`, and seven near misses are recorded as
REFUSED with the reason. One of them -- Greensand against Greenstore, two Danish
North Sea stores owned by the same two companies, one letter apart -- is the
sharpest argument in this repository for that rule.
NOTHING HERE EDITS A ROW. What a match produces is a rung 4 cell in the computed
ladder and, where the funder knows something the row does not, a queue line.
reader: sources/funder_search.py, and sources/cache/funders/index.json is its record

funders.programme: Innovation Fund — the funder's own project table, every call
funders.covers: every Innovation Fund call to date, all sectors, the EEA — so it covers all five ladder populations
funders.what_it_states: project, call, category, sector, location, technology pathway and status; the factsheet adds the coordinator, the grant amount, the expected avoidance and the start, financial-close and operation dates
funders.what_it_does_not_state: the site. The table gives a country and the factsheet gives a country; the site appears in the factsheet's prose where it appears at all, which is why every match here quotes it.

funders.programme: IPCEI on Batteries (SA.54793) and European Battery Innovation / EuBatIn (SA.55855)
funders.covers: nineteen Member States across the two, 59 companies
funders.outcome: READ AND NOT ENUMERABLE, and that is a finding about the publisher. The Commission's own page for the two battery IPCEIs states the Member States, the company counts (17 and 42) and the aid ceilings (EUR 3.2 bn and EUR 2.9 bn) AND NAMES NO COMPANY. The participant infographics are .zip archives and the decisions are PDFs at competition-cases; neither yields a participant list to a declared reader. So no battery entry can be scored `pass` from these two programmes, and none is scored `fail` from them either: the list was reached and its contents were not, which is `unread` about the funder, not a finding about any plant. Contrast the four hydrogen IPCEIs, whose participant infographics ARE readable and which brief 12 scored from.

refused_matches.nearly_matched: gem:P100000120638 Ferriera Valsabbia Odolo steel plant
refused_matches.why: REFUSED. The coordinator is Ferriera Valsabbia Spa, which is the works' owner, and the fiche places the project at 'hot rolling mills for steel bars in Brescia, Italy'. Odolo is in the province of Brescia and is not Brescia, and the owner runs more than one mill. A coordinator that matches and a site that only nearly does is the shape the match rule exists to refuse.

REFUSED, AND IT IS THE NEAREST MISS IN THIS PASS. The register holds BOTH `greensand` (INEOS Energy, Harbour Energy) and `greenstore` (Harbour Energy, INEOS Energy, Nordsøfonden) — two Danish North Sea stores, the same two companies, names one letter apart. The award names Greensand and Nini West, so it lands on `greensand`. Matched by the funder's own project name; a name fold would have hit both.
